summary: Takanori Fukita specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied as a graduate student at Bukkyo University (attested 2017) and held an appointed lecturer post at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Takanori Shintani is a scholar in religious studies and Japanology who studied at Waseda University (ca. 1968–1977). He held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (ca. 1999–2010) and Kokugakuin University (ca. 2010).

Takanori Unno, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his doctorate at Nagoya University, studying under teachers including Yoshifumi Ueda and Hidenori Kitagawa. He served as an assistant at Nagoya University, lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University, and professor at Meijo University (ca. 1988–2007).

Takao Hayashi specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University, Kyoto University, and Brown University (Ph.D. 1985 under David Pingree). His appointments include lecturer at Kyoto Women's University (1985–1987) and professor at Doshisha University (1995–2015).
Takao Kagawa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

Takao Maruyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (ca. 1957–1962). He held teaching posts at Rissho University (attested 1972, 1981), Shinshu University (attested 1983–1984; emeritus attested 2001), and Mejiro University (attested 1988).

Takao Moriyasu was a historian of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University (Doctor of Letters, 1992). He taught as an associate professor at Kanazawa University and Osaka University, where he was professor from 1994 to 2012.

Takao Yamagata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (ca. 1951–1955). He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (ca. 1966–2002) and served as president of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

Takashi Iwata, specializing in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg (Dr. Phil. under Albrecht Wezler and Lambert Schmithausen). He served as associate professor (ca. 1988–1993) and professor (ca. 1993–2014) at Waseda University.
Takashi Koezuka is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who held positions as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2012) at Osaka University.
Takashi Maeda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995 and 2006).

Takashi Matsuura is a linguistics and Indology scholar who earned his B.A. (2005) and Ph.D. (2021) from the University of Tokyo. He became an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo in 2022 and has taught at several institutions.

Takashi Nakao was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education (Doctor of Letters, 1974). He served as an associate professor at Bunkyo University Women's College and emeritus professor at Rissho University (1979–2002).

Takashi Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University, Peking University, and the University of Tokyo (Doctor of Letters, 2009). He served as associate professor at Komazawa University (1991) and specially appointed professor at Tokyo International University (2024).
Takashi Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University. He served as an associate professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (attested 2003).
Takatoshi Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1981 and 1991).
Takatoshi Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979. He served as a researcher at the Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute at Taisho University (attested 1978).

Takatsugu Hayashi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Delhi. His academic appointments include posts at Sendai National College of Technology, Hosen Gakuen College, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Takayasu Higuchi was an archaeology and Central Asian/Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (ca. 1939–1942). He was Professor of Archaeology at Kyoto University (ca. 1963–1982) and later directed Sen-oku Hakuko Kan and the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara.

Takayasu Kimura is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. In 1995, he was attested as a lecturer at Taisho University and researcher at the Institute of Modern Religious Education of Shingon Buzan.
